findings.summary: Token lifetime is 8 days by default, while the story says about a week.

Wrong password and unknown email are refused identically, but a deactivated account gets a different message ('Inactive user') once the correct password is given, so a correct password reveals account state. The story does not settle this.
Negative skip or limit is passed straight to the database OFFSET/LIMIT with no validation, which will likely raise a database error and return 500.
limit has no upper bound, so one request can return an unbounded number of items.
Sending title: null on update sets the title to None. The title column is non-nullable, so the commit will likely fail and return 500 instead of a 422.
Other users' items return 403 while missing items return 404, so a caller can tell whether an item id exists. The story says only that the item cannot be seen, changed or deleted.

A password-reset token is signed with the same key and has a sub that is an email, not a user id. Presented as a Bearer token, it passes signature checks and then session.get with a non-UUID sub likely raises a database error (500) instead of a 403.
Access tokens are not invalidated by a password change or reset. Tokens issued before the change stay valid until they expire.
Password-reset tokens are not single-use. They stay valid for 48 hours and can be reused to set the password repeatedly.
Token failure statuses are not specified. An expired or malformed token returns 403, a token for a deleted user returns 404, and a token for an inactive user returns 400.
Item description has a 255-character limit that the story does not mention.
Item titles are not unique per owner, so duplicate titles are accepted. The story does not say whether they should be.
Admin user-management routes (list, create, update, delete users) and password recovery and reset routes are not in the story.
The development-only private create_user has no authentication and no duplicate-email check, so a duplicate email will likely raise an integrity error (500).
